_provenance.coefficients: as shipped: full_ensemble when NGS present, V1_RATING_ONLY otherwise
_provenance.method: walk-forward; ratings use only weeks before each game
_provenance.scope_correction: Corrected twice. The first version graded V1_RATING_ONLY with no de-bias -- neither is what ships. Both errors were the same shape: measuring a simpler thing than the board runs.
_provenance.debias: applied, as the board does (median slate residual added to every model number)

pooled.note: see shipped.by_threshold; pooled over all games is not the bet the board makes

why_not_withheld: Totals were withheld on three findings at once: pooled below 50%, worse MAE than the market, and predictions compressed enough that 81% of their disagreement was explained by the market's own number. Spreads share the MAE concern; the Play threshold is above 50% rather than below, and its interval contains breakeven. That is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and withholding the whole board on it is a larger call than the evidence carries.

elo_gap.finding: The NGS fix restored the rating and dropped Elo: the full-ensemble vector carries elo_diff=0.0348, the rating-only vector has no elo_diff at all, so the live board has none.
elo_gap.dissociation: The better margin model is WORSE against the spread (44.6% vs 47.6% at Lean). A model that predicts better agrees with the market more, and the market is more accurate, so it disagrees less often and is wrong when it does. Accuracy and edge are different quantities.

mixed_path_slates.concern: Both vectors predict margins in points, so they are not unit-incompatible, but held out the rating-only path's predictions have sd 3.880 against ~5.8 for one carrying Elo. A single 4.0-point threshold is applied to gaps drawn from two distributions.
mixed_path_slates.harm_today: the lone rating-only game's gap is -0.23; nothing flags

compression_claim_withdrawn: The first version argued the model's predictions were compressed (sd 3.79 vs the market's 6.24). That was the rating-only path. The shipped model has sd 5.81 against 6.24 -- the spread model is NOT a near-constant fading market extremes the way the totals model demonstrably is.

debias_sweep.evidence: no slate in 2016-2025 weeks 4-17 had fewer than 8 priced games
debias_sweep.effect: de-bias helps modestly: play tier 51.18% -> 52.53% on the rating-only path
